body:
I’ve been a user for years. Edited to add: I do see that the developer usually responds to reviews, which I appreciate. But I am not open to submitting a feature request or sending screen recordings. You already know how the feature works; your PM (or someone) chose not to prioritize building an off switch for it despite it being a predictably disruptive feature. title: Worth the money!
body:
I downloaded this app to try a long while ago — I think a couple labor days ago?? — and right after I downloaded it, I got a notification saying they had a premium lifetime subscription on sale. On a whim, I decided to buy it and crossed my fingers it would be a good investment because it looked exactly like the kind of habit tracker I had been searching for. 

I’m happy to report that it was well worth the money for me, I love this app! It’s super customizable so you can track any habit however you want. And you can set up any kind of notification you’d like to receive (or not receive). There’s something so satisfying about ticking habits off the list, and being able to see calendar views of my progress is fun. It also syncs with Apple Health and my Apple Watch, though, I admit I haven’t really used that feature much. 

If you’re looking for a simple list-style app that you can use to check off habits and track progress, this is definitely the app for you! And if you see the lifetime subscription on sale, I definitely recommend jumping on it!

title: Ruined Widgets
body: It really pains me to write this. I loved using this app for all it offers, even bought the lifetime subscription because of it. However, after the most recent widget update, it’s been ruined. Widgets that used to be very helpful to track, especially being able to see which days I had off from specific tasks, are now ruined. I can no longer track when I have days off or my streak by simply looking at the widget. It was replaced by an “in progress” writing that then changed to “completed”. No streak counter, no days to see when to do the task. The colors have also changed on the widgets and it just makes the overall feel and look of using the app undesirable. On top of that, the widget used to display a +1 indicator to help me see that I had more sets to do on a certain task. It also kept track of my progress from the widget. That has now been removed and replaced by a dialog box that asks you how many times you’ve done the activity. The problem is that it doesn’t show the progress unless you look at the app. Defeats the purpose of a widget to me. If you do two sets and then forget that you did two, you go back to the widget which no longer shows your progress on it for the day. When you press on the widget it shows you the same “how many did you do” question. If you don’t remember it’s like starting over. It’s annoying. I thought the widgets and whole app were perfect and incredibly helpful but this last update really made me start looking for other habit-tracking apps.

title: Mixed Bag
body:
Habitify is one of the best habit trackers available. It syncs with Apple Health, allows editing on both a computer and a phone, and enables sharing habits with an accountability buddy. The app offers flexibility to track various types of habits, including minutes and times, and features a built-in timer for time-based habits. Additionally, it allows you to set a prior date as the start date and backfill the achievement of the habit, a feature many habit trackers lack.

However, there are some drawbacks. Apple Health habits can't be tracked for a full year; after six months, tracking stops, requiring you to archive the habit and start over. The app also frequently logs activities like meditation for 10 minutes but doesn't mark the habit as complete. To resolve this, you need to manually add extra time in Apple Health. Despite contacting support, they only explain the app's limitations without offering a solution.

I’d rather see the completed:skip options show up right away, before is it done or not instead of after. 

The only other complaint is no possibility for longer habit cycles. The habits are tied to specific days. That’s not great for the neurodivergent brain. I’d love the ability to track habit over a week. There are loads of things I need to do at least once a week but trying to force them weekly (eg must be Tuesday rather than at least once but could be any day) makes me less likely to do them. It means I need to keep some other list outside of the app and make the in-app habit really generic (like “exercise” with some external weekly specific exercise list) and then I have no way of tracking things like do I habitually ignore particular exercises.

title: Unsubscribe
body:
This app doesn’t give clear direction on how to opt out of email marketing, which violates the law -

One such law is the US’s CAN-SPAM legislation. This law, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission, states clearly that you must include a clearly obvious way for subscribers to opt out of your commercial messages:

Tell recipients how to opt out of receiving future email from you. Your message must include a clear and conspicuous explanation of how the recipient can opt out of getting email from you in the future. Craft the notice in a way that’s easy for an ordinary person to recognize, read, and understand. Creative use of type size, color, and location can improve clarity. Give a return email address or another easy Internet-based way to allow people to communicate their choice to you. You may create a menu to allow a recipient to opt out of certain types of messages, but you must include the option to stop all commercial messages from you. Make sure your spam filter doesn’t block these opt-out requests.

body: The app works fine, but you only get three habits to track and then it asks you for money. Alternatively you can buy the entire program for a one time fee of $50 or pay a monthly fee of $5 (which again should be a one time cost for the entire program). Let's be clear here; this is an app that sends reminders to you and gives you a virtual high five when you've accomplished your task. That's it. Nothing fancy about any of it. The interface is nice, but is it worth $50? Absolutely not. There are over 200 ratings on this app; if hypothetically 200 people liked the program enough to spend 10 dollars on it that would mean the programmers would have made somwhere around $20,000 dollars and I can guarantee you that it took a fraction of that to actually make this thing. The price point on this program is absoletely ludicrous, and it would appear the main habit the developers wish to instill in users is the one that puts money into their (devs) pockets. Hard pass from me.

I do have some minor requests:

2. With timers, could you make it so when you end the habit early it doesn’t discard your entire session? This isn’t that big of a deal as I rarely use the desktop app - but would be nice to have it completely synced with the iOS apps

This app contains two main ingredients that lead to personal success. Habit formation and metrics. 

1) Habit formation:
This app helps you form habits, small incremental life improvements geared toward your larger life goals. These habits are gamified by “streaks” or elongated periods of time in which you crush your daily habits multiple days in a row. 

2) Metric:
What can be measured can be improved. This app has got metrics and info galore. It helps me see if I falter, how well I’m doing and is direct correlated with the question. “Am I working towards my life goals”

Lastly, I’d pair this with actually thinking about your life and the big changes that you want to make in it.

An interesting feature allows you to set a time period for each habit in which to record your progress. A focus feature shows only those habits due for morning, afternoon, or evening, as well as those due anytime during the day. I don't use the focus feature, so it's annoying that I have to turn it off each time I open the app. It would be better to leave it in the same state it was when I exited the app.

All that said, the app doesn't have an interface that delights me and makes me want to use it every day.
